title: Ephemeral Prompt Bloom Bridge + GPU Slot Reuse for Near-Duplicate Prefix Deduplication
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Problem: The KV/prefix cache currently stores many near-duplicate prompt prefixes across tenants and sessions because small non-semantic differences (whitespace, tokenization boundary shifts, user metadata) prevent exact fingerprinting. This increases GPU resident memory usage and reduces effective hit rate for inter-request reuse, hurting tail latency and cost.

Proposal summary: Implement an Ephemeral Prompt Bloom Bridge (EPBB) — a small, probabilistic pre-index that sits in front of the canonical prefix registry to surface likely-duplicate prefixes quickly. EPBB combines a lightweight tenant-aware Bloom index with a short-lived compacted fragment pool kept in a soft GPU-resident slot. When a request arrives, the pipeline probes EPBB for candidates; on match we perform a delta-apply patch reconstruct (minimal KV reads) and opportunistically promote merged fragments into the shared pool. The design favors conservative false positives (Bloom) with a cheap secondary similarity check (token-simhash/minhash over normalized token stream) to avoid incorrect reuse.

Goals: reduce GPU KV footprint for hot prefixes, increase cross-request prefix hits (including near-duplicates), preserve correctness (no change to model outputs beyond acceptable risk), and integrate cleanly with continuous batching and prefetch paths.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce GPU-resident KV memory attributable to prefix fragments by >= 15% on mixed production workloads (p95)
Increase cross-request prefix reuse hit-rate by >= 10% for workloads with templated prompts (conversational assistants / code generation)
End-to-end 95th percentile latency for online inference does not regress by more than 3% vs baseline under identical load
False-positive reuse incidents must be < 0.5% and verified by automated diff/metric checks; rollbacks should be possible via feature-flag
Feature gated behind runtime flag, canaryed to 5% of traffic and validated before broader rollout
implementation_steps: Write a 2–3 page design doc describing EPBB architecture, index formats, and integration points with batching/kv-layer (owner: Liam)
Prototype Bloom + simhash probe in a test harness against 1 week of anonymized production traces (owner: SRE bench)
Define canonicalization rules (token normalization, template slot masking) and add unit tests covering edge cases (owner: Tokenization team)
Implement EPBB read-path integration in serving runtime: probe -> secondary simhash check -> delta-apply or canonical lookup (owner: runtime-optim)
Add GPU soft-pool manager: slot leasing, crediting, and eviction hooks tied to existing slab allocator (owner: gpu-mem)
Performance run: A/B perf + cost run on dedicated cluster; collect GPU mem, tail latency, hit-rate, and error diffs (owner: perf)
Safety checks: output-diff harness comparing model outputs for reused vs fresh KV reads on a suite of 2k golden prompts (owner: evals)
Canary rollout: feature-flag, start at 1% traffic -> 5% -> 20% while monitoring key metrics and SLOs (owner: rollout)
Documentation + console observability: add EPBB metric tiles and debugging trace links in Console (owner: observability)
Post-mortem and tuning: iterate on Bloom sizing, simhash thresholds, and slot-credit policy based on canary data
decisions: Use tenant-aware Bloom filters to reduce cross-tenant false positives; a tenant id salt is part of the filter key
Perform a cheap secondary similarity check using simhash over normalized token ids before trusting a Bloom hit
Delta-apply patch format chosen instead of full-fragment copy to minimize GPU read bandwidth; patch contains token ranges + replacement ops
Soft-resident pool uses credited leasing (time + access count) rather than strict LRU to prefer fragments that are reused across batches
Conservative defaults: small Bloom (2–4 KB per tenant shard) and simhash Hamming threshold tuned to favor recall while bounding FP rate
